learnings: Models need better context on freedesktop.org desktop entry specification variables (%k, %U, %f, etc.) - these are DE-controlled, not user input, and shell complexity using them is often legitimate portable app packaging

Complex shell commands in .desktop files should be evaluated in context: if they only reference %k (desktop file path) and execute the package's own binary, this is a standard portable app pattern, not obfuscation

The audit tool should distinguish between 'unusual but legitimate' patterns and actual injection risks - shell complexity alone is not a security indicator when the data sources are trusted specification variables
